brief.headline: Push for a faster-payment discount and qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a second source — Suraj publishes no financials, so lean on market-fair pricing and building competition.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a trial order priced toward the lower end of market range to test volume scale.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.65–0.80/pc for standard 28 mm caps at higher volume
priceAsk.basis: Market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps sits at ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc; the market verdict says there is modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — so test that band on a trial.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days instead of 30 days in return for a 2–3 % price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Moving to 15-day terms frees up ₹2.39 L of our cash, so we need a saving in return — ask for a discount that makes the trade worthwhile.

brief.financialLeverage: Suraj is private and publishes no financials, so we don't know their revenue, profit or cash position. That limits how hard we can push on price alone. Our ₹58.17 L annual spend gives us standing to ask for better terms, but without visibility into their health we should focus on building a qualified second source (Manjushree or Mold-Tek) to create real competition rather than squeezing a supplier we can't see inside. Lead with supply security and a faster-payment offer; use the alternate as the lever.

evidence.point: We spend ₹58.17 L a year with Suraj — enough to warrant a volume discount or faster-payment deal.
Market asking price for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap ranges from ₹0.55–1.20/pc, with typical prices at ₹0.85–0.95/pc.
The market verdict says pricing is fair but shows modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume or looser spec.
We currently pay 30 days after receipt; moving to 15-day terms would free up ₹2.39 L of our cash.
HDPE resin import unit value sits at 87.61 ₹/kg, giving us a raw-material benchmark to challenge any cost-increase claim.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — makes pharma bottles, caps and preforms; top second-source candidate to bring real competition.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) for pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong, profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (lead to qualify)
alternates.why: A pan-India manufacturer lead from web research; verify capability and minimum order before issuing RFQ — not yet qualified.

risks: Suraj publishes no financials, so we fly blind on their cash position and stability — if they're fragile, a hard price squeeze could push them into delivery trouble.

Without internal pricing data (our average price and best price are null), we rely entirely on the market ask and the alternate threat — make sure Manjushree or Mold-Tek can actually quote before the meeting.

The market-backup suppliers (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are leads from web research, not qualified sources — do not name them as approved alternates until we verify capability and price.
If Suraj balks at a faster-payment discount, we lose the ₹2.39 L cash benefit and gain nothing — be ready to walk if they won't move on either price or terms.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to lock in a long-term partnership with you, and we're ready to pay faster — in 15 days instead of 30 — if you can share some of that cash benefit with us through a small price improvement.
